design.name: 火浣鼠
design.brief: A mythical fire rat (火鼠) whose fur is woven into fireproof cloth in Chinese legend: a round, chubby rat with a thick coat of bristling fur that burns at the tips with white-gold flames, small fierce glowing eyes, big front teeth, a long fiery tail, little paws with four toes. Shown both standing and curled into a rolling ball of fire. Cute and explosive.
design.turnaround_pose: standing ON ALL FOURS like a real rat (quadruped, NOT upright, NOT on its hind legs): real rat anatomy and proportions but slightly chubby and stylized: a long rounded body held low and horizontal, the back gently arched, a pointed snout with the two big front teeth showing, round ears, fierce glowing eyes; all four legs straight under the body and planted on the ground in a neutral stance, front paws and hind feet clearly separated; the long tail extending straight backwards and rising slightly upward behind the body (not curled, not over the back); ALL flames are drawn as OPAQUE solid sculpted flame-shaped fur tufts with crisp edges (stylized carved fur that looks like flames, red-orange with pale gold tips), a flame crest on the head and a ridge of flame tufts along the spine, NOT transparent fire, NO glow halo, NO sparks, NO smoke, NO particles; never a rolled-up ball
design.turnaround_digits: each front paw with four separate clawed toes and each hind foot with five separate clawed toes, clearly countable; the whole tail, both ears, the snout and every flame tuft fully inside the frame; in the side views the long body and tail must fit inside the view with margin.
